newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN FOREIGN MINISTER GOES TO S.AFRICA ON MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN FOREIGN MINISTER GOES TO S.AFRICA ON MONDAY.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign minister will leave for South Africa on Monday to discuss the future of bilateral relations following Pretoria's plan to switch ties to Beijing, the foreign ministry said.

The ministry said minister John Chang would meet his Pretoria counterpart, Alfred Nzo, during the five-day visit and would use the visit to examine cooperative projects between the two sides in South Africa.

"Aside from negotiating with South Africa's high-level government officials concerning bilateral relations, (Chang) also will examine all the projects in Pretoria involving cooperation with Taiwan," ministry spokesman Peter Cheng told reporters.
Cheng said it was uncertain whether the minister would hold talks with President Nelson Mandela.
Mandela said on Wednesday that Pretoria, a longtime diplomatic ally of Taiwan, would switch formal ties to Beijing by the end of 1997.
The move shocked increasingly isolated Taiwan.
Chang originally had scheduled the Pretoria visit for January, but brought the trip forward due to the diplomatic fallout. He plans to return to Taiwan on December 8.
Since Pretoria's announcement Taiwan said it would stop encouraging investments in South Africa and would re-evaluate economic loans and aid previously made for diplomatic purposes.
Nearly 300 Taiwan businesses have operations in South Africa with investments topping US$1.5 billion.
